hints: Express $\tan\theta$ as $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and multiply through by $\cos\theta$ to get $4\sin^2\theta = \cos\theta + 5\cos^2\theta$.
Solve for $\cos\theta$ using the quadratic formula, and find all four solutions in $-180^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Replace $\tan\theta$ with $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and multiply through by $\cos\theta$:
$$4\sin\theta\left(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = 1 + 5\cos\theta \implies 4\sin^2\theta = \cos\theta + 5\cos^2\theta$$

Substitute the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta$ and form a standard quadratic in $\cos\theta$:
$$4(1 - \cos^2\theta) = \cos\theta + 5\cos^2\theta \implies 4 - 4\cos^2\theta = \cos\theta + 5\cos^2\theta \implies 9\cos^2\theta + \cos\theta - 4 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula to solve for $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1^2 - 4(9)(-4)}}{2(9)} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{145}}{18}$$
$$\cos\theta_1 \approx 0.61342 \quad\text{and}\quad \cos\theta_2 \approx -0.72453$$

Calculate the solutions within the interval $-180^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} \cos\theta = 0.61342: &\quad \theta = \pm\arccos(0.61342) \approx \pm 52.2^\circ \\ \cos\theta = -0.72453: &\quad \theta = \pm\arccos(-0.72453) \approx \pm 136.4^\circ \end{aligned}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Uses $\tan\theta=\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta$ to derive $9\cos^2\theta+\cos\theta-4=0$, solves for $\cos\theta$, and finds $\pm 52.2^\circ, \pm 136.4^\circ$.
